summary: Robin Dunbar studied at Magdalen College School, Magdalen College (~1966–1969), and under doctoral supervisor John Hurrell Crook (~1969–1974). He held a post at University College London from ~1987 to 1994.

Philosopher Roderick M. Chisholm studied at Brown University (1934–1938) and Harvard (Ph.D. ~1938–1942). He taught at the Barnes Foundation (~1946) and Brown (~1947–1986), also serving as president of the Metaphysical Society of America in 1973.
Working in Buddhist and religious studies, Roderick S. Bucknell held positions at the University of Queensland, starting around 1976 and serving as associate professor (attested 1999–2000).

Specializing in history, archaeology, sinology, and Buddhist studies, Roderick Whitfield held posts at the British Museum (attested 1986) and SOAS University of London, where he was Professor Emeritus (attested 2011) and active through at least 2022.

A scholar of Buddhist studies, Roger Bischoff studied under traditional teachers Mother Sayamagyi and U Chit Tin. He served as an assistant teacher at the International Meditation Centre (attested 1995).
Linguist Roger Brown studied at the University of Michigan (~1945–1952) and held a post at Harvard University from 1962 to 1994.

Roger Heim studied at École Centrale Paris (~1920–1923) and the Science Faculty of Paris (until 1931). He held a post at the Muséum National d'Histoire Naturelle (~1929–1970), serving as its director from ~1950 to 1965.

Scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology Roger R. Jackson earned degrees from Wesleyan and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (Ph.D. 1983). He taught at Fairfield University (attested 1986) and Carleton College (attested 1990–2017).

Philosopher and sinologist Roger T. Ames earned degrees from UBC, NTU, and SOAS under D. C. Lau. He served as professor at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (1978–2016) and editor of Philosophy East and West (~1987–2016).
Rohit Saluja works in computational fields and Indology, holding posts at the Indian Institute of Technology Mandi and BharatGen.

Philosopher and linguist Roland Barthes studied at the Faculty of Arts of Paris (~1935–1939) and under Émile Benveniste. He held posts at the CNRS (~1952–1959), the EHESS (~1962–1976), and the Collège de France (1976–1980).
Historian, archaeologist, and Indologist Roland Ferenczi is attested in 2026 as a visiting lecturer at Eötvös Loránd University and a project researcher at the University of Hamburg.
Working in Indology and Tibetology, Roland Steiner studied under Michael Hahn (attested 1990) and served as assistant professor at the University of Marburg (attested 2002).

Historian Roland Wenzlhuemer studied at the University of Salzburg and Heidelberg University. His posts include the Leibniz-Zentrum Moderner Orient (~2002–2005), Humboldt University (~2005–2008), Heidelberg University (2008, 2014), and the University of Munich (2017).

Tibetologist and sinologist Rolf Alfred Stein studied under Chavannes, Pelliot, Maspero, and Demiéville, among others. He was directeur d'études at the EPHE (1951–1975) and professor at the Collège de France (1965–1982).
Specializing in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Rolf Scheuermann completed a Magister der Philosophie at the University of Vienna under supervisor Helmut Tauscher (attested 2010).

Historian and Indologist Romila Thapar studied under A. L. Basham at SOAS (doctorate ~1955–1958). She held professorships at the University of Delhi (1963–1970) and Jawaharlal Nehru University (1970–1991, 1993).
Working in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Ron Garry studied under traditional teachers Lama Tharchin Rinpoche and Tulku Thubten Rinpoche.
Ron Leifer, active in Buddhist studies and other fields, studied under Agehananda Bharati in 1964 and under the traditional teacher Khenpo Karthar Rinpoche.

Working in Tibetology and sociology, Ronald D. Schwartz held positions as Professor of Sociology at Memorial University of Newfoundland (attested 1998) and Honorary Research Fellow at the University of Hong Kong.
